title: The Tin Box
text:
My grandmother kept her recipes in a tin box that smelled faintly of cloves. I remember her hands, always dusted with flour, moving with a certainty I have never managed to recover. She rarely wrote anything down, preferring to let the measurements live in her memory. When I finally opened the box after her funeral, I found only three cards, and their handwriting was unsteady.

Those three cards became the foundation of a project I could not abandon. I spent a winter attempting to reproduce each dish, failing repeatedly and recording every mistake. The exercise taught me less about cooking than about the ways memory fills gaps with feeling rather than fact. Some dishes I reconstructed; others I accepted as lost, and I came to see the missing details as a kind of inheritance.
